messages:
marta (sales-eng): Hey team, POC with AcmeCorp is blocked — their app can't connect to our private endpoint in their VPC. Customer sees TLS handshake failure and 403s. They said it worked for a few minutes then died. attaching logs below. can we triage?

omar (eng): Can you paste the curl -v output / tcpdump? Also is this an interface endpoint or gateway endpoint?

marta (sales-eng): It's an interface endpoint (AWS ENI). Here's curl from their app host (redacted IPs):

```
curl -v https://private-infer.redwood.internal/predict 
* Rebuilt URL to: https://private-infer.redwood.internal/predict
*   Trying 10.0.5.23...
* TCP_NODELAY set
* Connected to private-infer.redwood.internal (10.0.5.23) port 443 (#0)
* ALPN, offering http/1.1
* Cipher selection: ALL
* SSL connection using TLSv1.2 / ECDHE-RSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256
* Server certificate: CN=corp-proxy.local, O=Corp Inc
* server certificate verification OK
* TLSv1.2 (OUT), TLS handshake, Client hello (1)
* SSL: certificate subject name 'corp-proxy.local' does not match 'private-infer.redwood.internal'
* Closing connection 0
* SSL: certificate subject name 'corp-proxy.local' does not match 'private-infer.redwood.internal'
* Curl failed to verify the legitimacy of the server and therefore could not
* establish a secure connection to it.
* Closing connection 0
```

marta (sales-eng): tcpdump shows SYN/ACK then TLS ClientHello but cert returned is our customer's corporate proxy cert. customer says they have TLS inspection in place.

elaine (netops): 2 quick things to confirm: 1) is the customer's private hosted zone resolving to the interface endpoint ENI (10.0.5.23) rather than a public IP? 2) are there any NAT/firewall rules doing TLS interception? if they have a transparent proxy it will break hostname validation.

liam (solutions): If it is TLS inspection, the proxy re-signs certs with an internal CA — app needs that CA in its truststore. Alternatively recommend mutual TLS (mTLS) between app and our endpoint or put the endpoint in a dedicated subnet with forced egress rules to skip the proxy.

omar (eng): For quick triage: ask customer to `openssl s_client -connect 10.0.5.23:443 -servername private-infer.redwood.internal -showcerts` and paste first cert subject. If the cert CN is not our SAN, it's interception. Also check `dig private-infer.redwood.internal @10.0.0.2` (their resolver) to verify split-horizon.

marta (sales-eng): pasted result from openssl: cert shows CN=corp-proxy.local, issuer=Corp Internal CA. so definitely MITM. customer says their security team enforces HTTPS inspection for all egress.

elaine (netops): Two remediation paths: 1) Customer adds exception for the endpoint CIDR in their TLS inspection appliance (recommended), or 2) customer uploads Corp Internal CA to the app's JVM/container truststore (if they control the app image). Also make sure security groups on the ENI allow their proxy ip ranges (if proxy is outbound).

liam (solutions): Additional option: we can provision a dedicated private endpoint that uses mutual TLS and validates client certs — that bypasses truststore issues. That is a Dedicated/enterprise feature, estimate adds to timeline and pricing.

omar (eng): Practical checklist to send customer:
- Confirm DNS resolves to interface endpoint ENI (private IP)
- Paste `openssl s_client -connect <ip>:443 -servername private-infer.redwood.internal -showcerts` output
- Confirm presence of TLS inspection / proxy and whether they can add an exception for our endpoint CIDR
- If they can't change proxy, add their proxy CA to the app truststore, or request mTLS from us (we'll need their client cert CSR)
- Ensure egress to OCSP/CRL and our cert chain endpoints are not blocked (ports 80/443 to ocsp/root endpoints)

marta (sales-eng): I'll send checklist. quick q for pricing: if they need dedicated endpoint/mTLS, how much uplift vs hosted?

liam (solutions): DM me the deal size, but short answer: dedicated/private endpoint with mTLS is a Dedicated plan add-on with monthly reserved capacity pricing — expect 2-3x baseline hosted unit cost depending on committed GPU capacity. I can draft a proposal once we confirm requirements.

deploy-bot: deployment completed: private-endpoint-config v2 pushed to staging at 2026-03-15T16:42:10Z 

omar (eng): Note — also confirm their proxy isn't rewriting SNI (some appliances do). If SNI is stripped/replaced, TLS validation will fail even with CA present. Ask them to capture TLS ClientHello SNI.

marta (sales-eng): Thanks all — I'll escalate to their security team and ask for exception or CA bundle. will update thread when they respond. :thumbsup:
